Prussia: German state from 1525 to 1947. Prussia (German: Preußen [ˈpʁɔʏsn̩]; Old Prussian: Prūsija) was a German state centred on the North European Plain.
A Bosnian Serb commander of the Army of Republika Srpska during the Yugoslav Wars, he's now serving a life sentence in The Hague for genocide and crimes against humanity — who is he?
This American author built a personal-finance empire around his bestselling Rich Dad Poor Dad book series, even as one of his companies filed for bankruptcy in 2012 — who is he?
Robert Kiyosaki: American finance author and investor (born 1947)
An Iraqi politician who served as the fifth president from 1979 until his overthrow in 2003 during the US-led invasion, previously a vice president and prime minister—who was he?
Saddam Hussein: President of Iraq from 1979 to 2003. The policies and ideologies he championed are collectively known as Saddamism, a right-wing variant of Ba'athism.
This Sanskrit term, meaning 'wandering' or 'running around in circles,' describes the ongoing cycle of life, death, and rebirth central to Indian religious philosophy — what is it called?
Saṃsāra: Indian concept of the cyclical process of death and rebirth.
Daughter of Bangladesh's first president, she became the country's longest-serving prime minister and one of the world's longest-serving female heads of government — who is she?
Sheikh Hasina: Prime Minister of Bangladesh (1996–2001; 2009–2024)
Established as a client state of Nazi Germany in March 1939, this Central European nation's army also joined the invasion of Poland that year — which state, whose capital was Bratislava?
Slovak Republic (1939–1945): Client state of Nazi Germany. The Slovak part of Czechoslovakia declared independence with German support one day before the German occupation of Bohemia and Moravia.
It's the season when the earliest sunrises and latest sunsets crowd around a single solstice — and when half the planet swelters, the other half shivers. Which season is it?
Summer: Hottest of the four temperate seasons.
Instituted by Diocletian in AD 293, this system split rule of the Roman Empire between two senior 'augusti' and two junior 'caesars' — what was it called?
Tetrarchy: Roman system of power division among four rulers.
A former Army officer, this Arkansas Republican unseated incumbent Mark Pryor in 2014 to become the state's junior U.S. senator — who is he?
Tom Cotton: American politician and veteran (born 1977)
Symbolizing both a diamond's indestructibility and a thunderbolt's force, this ritual scepter-like tool is used alongside a bell in Tibetan Buddhist ceremonies — what is it called?
Vajra: Spiritual weapon or symbol in Dharmic religions.
A key figure of Chile's Nueva Canción movement, this singer-songwriter was arrested and killed in the days following the 1973 coup that overthrew President Allende — who was he?
Víctor Jara: Chilean folk singer and activist (1932–1973)

Serving four non-consecutive terms as British Prime Minister between 1868 and 1894 — more than anyone else — this Liverpool-born statesman began as a Conservative MP before becoming the face of the Liberal Party — who was he?
Born in Georgia, this Red Army officer and engineer was the eldest son of a Bolshevik revolutionary who became head of the Soviet Union — who is he?
Yakov Dzhugashvili: Red Army officer and Joseph Stalin's son (1907–1943)
An early convert to Islam and a commander at the Battle of Badr in 624, this Arab Muslim general fought in the Ridda Wars and the early conquests of Persia, Syria and North Africa — who was he?
Zubayr ibn al-Awwam: Arab Muslim military commander (594–656)
Who among these was born first?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
William Osler (born 1849) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the oldest?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was founded earliest?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four. COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language;) is a compiled English-like computer programming language designed for business use.
Which of these is a physicist?
Max von Laue is a physicist.
Which of these is a chemist?
Alfred Nobel is a chemist. Alfred Bernhard Nobel ( noh-BEL; Swedish: [ˈǎlːfrɛd nʊˈbɛlː]; 21 October 1833 – 10 December 1896) was a Swedish chemist, inventor, engineer, and businessman.
What is the atomic number of Einsteinium?
Einsteinium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Es and atomic number 99 and is a member of the actinide series and the seventh transuranium element.
In what year was Hamish Harding born?
Hamish Harding: George Hamish Livingston Harding (24 June 1964 – 18 June 2023) was a British businessman, pilot and adventurer based in the United Arab Emirates (UAE).
In what year was Vikram Sarabhai born?
Vikram Sarabhai: Often regarded as the "Father of Indian space program", Sarabhai was honored with Padma Bhushan in 1966 and the Padma Vibhushan (posthumously) in 1972.
In what year was Johann Wolfgang von Goethe born?
Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (28 August 1749 – 22 March 1832) was a German polymath who is widely regarded as the most influential writer in the German language.
In what year did Aryabhata die?
Aryabhata: The claim that Nalanda used to be located in Kusamapura/Pataliputra also cannot be proven.
In what year did Ivan Pavlov die?
Ivan Pavlov: Pavlov also conducted significant research on the physiology of digestion, for which he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1904.
In what year was Iodine discovered?
Iodine is a chemical element; it has symbol I and atomic number 53.
In what year was Nickel discovered?
Nickel is a chemical element; it has symbol Ni and atomic number 28.
Magnesium sulfate: Pfizer. It is a white crystalline solid, soluble in water.
In which country is Fish and chips?
Fish and chips: United Kingdom. Fish and chips is a hot dish consisting of battered and fried fish, served with chips.
Who is credited with discovering Norma?

Norma (constellation): Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Its name is Latin for normal, referring to a right angle, and is variously considered to represent a rule, a carpenter's square, a set square or a level.
Who is credited with discovering Aspartame?
Aspartame: James M. Schlatter. Aspartame is an artificial, non-saccharide sweetener commonly used as a sugar substitute in foods and beverages.
Who is credited with discovering Histamine?
Histamine: Henry Hallett Dale. Histamine or histamin is an organic nitrogenous compound found in mammals and many vegetables, fruits and food products.
About 5 million tonnes of acetic acid are produced annually largely to make this compound, most commonly in polymer form — what is it?
Acetate is a salt formed by the combination of acetic acid with a base (e.g. sodium hydroxide), an ester of acetic acid, or the anion CH3COO- found in solution.
First approved in the United States in 1966, this xanthine oxidase inhibitor treats high uric acid levels linked to gout, kidney stones, and chemotherapy — what medication is it?
Allopurinol is a medication used to decrease high blood uric acid levels.
This symptom, not a diagnosis by itself, refers to a loss of appetite in humans and — under the name 'inappetence' — in animals from dogs to goats. Which symptom?
Anorexia (symptom) is a medical term for a loss of appetite.
The second-largest living lizard species after the Komodo dragon, native to South and Southeast Asia. It's a varanid found from India to the Indonesian islands. What is it?
Asian water monitor (Varanus salvator) is a large varanid lizard native to South and Southeast Asia.
Causing frequent urination and a weak stream, this noncancerous enlargement of a male gland isn't caused by poor hygiene and has no known cure, only symptom management. What condition is it?
Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), also called prostate enlargement, is a noncancerous increase in size of the prostate gland.
Belonging to the Colubridae family of venomous snakes and found only in Sub-Saharan Africa, this reptile's scientific name is Dispholidus typus — what is it commonly called?
Boomslang (or; Dispholidus typus) is a highly venomous snake in the family Colubridae.
This American actress is remembered chiefly as the mother of a famous Hollywood actress and actor, and the former wife of actor Jon Voight. Who is she?
Caesium (IUPAC spelling; also spelled cesium in American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Cs and atomic number 55.
Named for the whisker-like barbels many species sport, these scaleless ray-finned fish include some of the largest freshwater giants in Southeast Asia and Eurasia — name this diverse group of fish?
Catfish are a diverse group of ray-finned fish of the order Siluriformes (historically Nematognathi).
This insect family, known as the 'true' members of its group, contains roughly 3,400 species worldwide, distinct from just two species in a smaller sister family. What family is it?

Cicadidae is one of two families of cicadas, with about 3,400 species in over 520 genera worldwide; it contains most living cicada species, except for the two belonging to its sister taxon, the Tettigarctidae.

Serving as personal doctor to a superstar singer on the day of his 2009 death, this physician was later convicted of involuntary manslaughter over the misuse of a surgical anesthetic as a sleep aid — who is he?
Conrad Murray (born February 19, 1953) is a Grenadian-born American former physician convicted for his role in the death of American singer and dancer Michael Jackson.
Unrelated to poor hygiene, this scalp condition causes flaking and mild itching and is often treated with antifungal or keratolytic remedies; about half of all adults experience it. What is it?
Dandruff is a skin condition of the scalp. It can result in social or self-esteem problems.
Made from a fermented batter of ground black gram and rice, this thin South Indian bread is traditionally served with chutney and sambar — what is it?

Dosa (food) (in Indian English) or thosai (in Malaysian English and Singapore English) is a thin, savoury batter bread in South Indian cuisine made from a fermented batter of ground black gram and rice.
The tallest native bird in Australia and the third-tallest living bird overall, this flightless ratite can grow up to 1.9 metres tall. What bird is it?
Emu (Dromaius novaehollandiae) is a species of flightless bird endemic to Australia, where it is the tallest native bird.
Equivalent to one coulomb per volt, this SI unit of electrical capacitance is named after a pioneering English physicist — name the unit?
Farad (symbol: F) is the unit of electrical capacitance, the ability of a body to store an electrical charge, in the International System of Units (SI), equivalent to 1 coulomb per volt (C/V).
Having led Renault, Sauber, and Alfa Romeo's F1 outfits, this French engineer took the reins at Ferrari as team principal in 2023 — who is he?
Fred Vasseur (French; born 28 May 1968) is a French motorsport executive, businessman and engineer.
This pancreatic hormone kicks in when blood sugar dips too low, prompting the liver to convert stored glycogen back into glucose. What is it?
Glucagon is a peptide hormone, produced by alpha cells of the pancreas.
This Austrian physician wrote over 300 publications and termed his diagnosis of autism 'autistic psychopathy,' though later allegations tied him to a Nazi-era clinic in Vienna — what was his name?
Hans Asperger (18 February 1906 - 21 October 1980) was an Austrian physician.
Which cosmological relationship says a galaxy's recession speed is proportional to its distance from Earth, discovered via redshift measurements and usually credited to a 1929 paper?
Hubble's law is the observation in physical cosmology that galaxies are moving away from Earth at speeds proportional to their distance.
This post-transition metal, chemically similar to gallium and thallium, was identified spectroscopically in 1863 and takes its name from the indigo line in its spectrum — what element is it?
Indium is a chemical element; its symbol is In and its atomic number is 49.
Born in Albuquerque and a Princeton engineering graduate, this businessman founded and once ran Amazon, the e-commerce and cloud-computing giant — who is he?

Jeff Bezos (n Jorgensen; born January 12, 1964) is an American businessman, and the founder, executive chairman, and former president and CEO of Amazon, the world's largest e-commerce and cloud computing company.
Also called a kilopond, this deprecated gravitational metric unit equals exactly 9.80665 newtons — the weight of a one-thousand-gram mass under standard gravity. What is it?
Kilogram-force (kgf or kgF), or kilopond (kp, from Latin pondus, 'weight'), is a non-standard gravitational metric unit of force equal to the weight on Earth of a one-kilogram mass.
This leafy member of the daisy family is eaten raw in salads and sandwiches, though one Asian variety, celtuce, is grown instead for its edible stem — what is it?
Lettuce (Lactuca sativa) is an annual plant of the family Asteraceae mostly grown as a leaf vegetable.
Often caused by cigarette smoking or inhaled chemicals damaging airway cell DNA, this malignant tumor often shows no symptoms until it has already spread. What disease is it?
Lung cancer is a malignant tumor that originates in the tissues of the lungs.
Working on the geometry of Riemann surfaces, this Tehran-born Stanford professor became in 2014 the first woman and first Iranian to win the Fields Medal — who was she?
Maryam Mirzakhani (12 May 1977 - 14 July 2017) was an Iranian mathematician and a professor of mathematics at Stanford University.

Introduced in 1975 and still in production today at two Russian factories, this Soviet-designed helicopter family serves as both a medium twin-turbine transport and, in gunship form, an armed attack aircraft — what's the helicopter?

Mil Mi-17 (NATO reporting name: Hip) is a Soviet-designed Russian military helicopter family introduced in 1975 (Mi-8M), continuing in production as of 2024 at two factories in Russia, in Kazan and Ulan-Ude.

This symbiotic relationship between a fungus and a plant, in which fungal threads interconnect with plant roots at the cellular level, plays a major role in plant nutrition and soil chemistry — what is it called?
Sold in packs needing a desiccant to keep it from absorbing moisture, this seaweed sheet was once used as currency and shrine offerings in Japan — what is it?
Nori is a dried edible seaweed used in Japanese cuisine, usually made from species of the red algae genus Pyropia, including P. yezoensis and P. tenera.
Often linked to polycystic ovary syndrome or pelvic inflammatory disease, this fluid-filled sac can cause severe pain if it ruptures or twists — what is it?
Ovarian cyst is a fluid-filled sac within the ovary. If the cyst either breaks open or causes twisting of the ovary, it may cause severe pain.
Listed in the Dictionary of Fungi as containing over 300 species, this mold genus produces a compound that stops bacterial growth and also flavors certain cheeses — which genus?
Penicillium is a genus of ascomycetous fungi that is part of the mycobiome of many species and is of major importance in the natural environment, in food spoilage, and in food and drug production.
This scientific term for a group of fin-footed, mostly marine mammals includes walruses, sea lions, fur seals, and true earless seals — 34 living species in all. What is the term?
Pinniped are a widely distributed and diverse clade of carnivorous, fin-footed, semiaquatic, mostly marine mammals.
Lacking any real scientific definition, this British term for a large swimming crustacean has become almost interchangeable with 'shrimp' — what is it?
Prawn is a common name for small aquatic crustaceans with an exoskeleton and ten legs (members of the order of decapods), some of which are edible.

This small herbivore belongs to the family Leporidae alongside hares, and the European species of its genus has been introduced to every continent except Antarctica — what bouncy little prey animal is it?
Rabbit are small mammals in the family Leporidae (which also includes the hares), which is in the order Lagomorpha (which also includes pikas).
Made by steaming dehusked oat groats before flattening them under heavy rollers and lightly toasting them, this whole-grain food becomes porridge when cooked — which product?
Rolled oats are a type of lightly processed whole-grain food.

After early attempts at family-friendly Christian video games found little success, this American developer switched to horror in 2014 and created a hit franchise about animatronic mascots that come alive at night — who is he?

Scott Cawthon (born June 4, 1978) is an American video game developer, writer, and producer best known for creating Five Nights at Freddy's, a series of horror video games which expanded into a media franchise.
Marked by reduced muscle activity yet busy, active brain patterns, this state alternates between REM and non-REM cycles — what is it?
Sleep is a state of reduced mental and physical activity in which consciousness is altered and certain sensory activity is inhibited.

After more than 40 years at DuPont, this Polish-American chemist became the first woman to win the company's Lavoisier Medal — an honor that recognized her invention of a famously bullet-stopping fiber. Who was she?
Stephanie Kwolek (July 31, 1923 - June 18, 2014) was a Polish-American chemist known for inventing Kevlar (poly-paraphenylene terephthalamide).
This actress and singer's breakout role on Pretty Little Liars won her seven Teen Choice Awards, more than any actress in a single series. Who is she?
Tarragon (Artemisia dracunculus), also known as estragon, is a species of perennial herb in the family Asteraceae.
This intensely itchy, contagious fungal skin infection produces a red, scaly rash with a curved border across the groin and buttocks, mostly in men — what is it?

Tinea cruris (TC), also known as jock itch, is a common type of contagious, superficial fungal infection of the groin and buttocks region, which occurs predominantly but not exclusively in men and in hot-humid climates.
Medically called micturition or voiding, this voluntary process happens up to seven times a day in a healthy adult — and goes by "number one." What is it?
Urination is the release of urine from the bladder through the urethra in placental mammals, or through the cloaca in other vertebrates.

First cultivated in the Fertile Crescent around 9600 BC, this cereal grass genus is grown on more land worldwide than any other food crop, with varieties including spelt, durum, and einkorn — name the crop?
Wheat is a group of wild and domesticated grasses of the genus Triticum.
Launched in 1981 as a joint venture between French and Italian aerospace firms, this high-wing turboprop airliner later formed the basis for a stretched successor introduced in 1989 — which aircraft?
This mushroom genus of more than 400 species includes both the common button mushroom and the field mushroom, the two most-cultivated fungi in the West — which genus is it?
Also called ramsons or bear leek, this bulbous woodland plant native to Eurasia is a wild cousin of onion and garlic — what is it?
Allium ursinum: Species of flowering plant in the family Amaryllidaceae.
A branch of morphology with roots in prehistoric times, which natural science studies the internal and external structure of organisms and their parts?
Anatomy: Study of the structure of organisms. Anatomy is a branch of natural science that deals with the structural organization of living things.
Known by common names like greenfly and blackfly, these small sap-sucking insects reproduce via live-born nymphs without males, a trick called telescoping generations — what are they?
Aphid: Superfamily of insects. The group includes the fluffy white woolly aphids.
This chronic airway disease causes wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath when triggers like pollen or dust make the bronchioles constrict and fill with mucus — what condition is it?
Asthma: Long-term inflammatory disease of the airways of the lungs.
Also called Asian sea bass, this catadromous fish is widely distributed from the Middle East across South and Southeast Asia to Oceania — which fish?
Barramundi: Species of fish. The species is widely distributed in the Indo-West Pacific, spanning the waters of the Middle East, South Asia, Southeast Asia, East Asia, and Oceania.
This interdisciplinary field examines moral questions raised by advances in biology, medicine, and biotechnology, touching everything from patient care to environmental policy — what is it called?
Bioethics: Study of the ethical issues emerging from advances in biology and medicine.

Bred in South Africa as a family guard dog, this large mastiff-type breed has a short coat and heavy bone structure, and is recognized by that country's kennel union but not the international federation — what breed is it?
Boerboel: South African breed of dog. The Boerboel (pronounced [ˈbuːrbul]) is a South African breed of large dog of mastiff type, used as a family guard dog.
An intact, more muscular and aggressive adult male of the cattle species, this animal has long been a sacrificial symbol in many religions and stars in famous arena sports. What is it?
Bull: Adult male cattle. A bull is an intact (i.e., not castrated) adult male of the species Bos taurus (cattle).
Also known as hemp when grown for fiber rather than its psychoactive use, this Asian-native plant genus includes up to three disputed species — which plant?
Also known as an Ovcharka, this large livestock-guardian breed was developed in the Soviet Union around 1920 from mountain and steppe animals of the Caucasus region — which breed?
Caucasian Shepherd Dog: Russian breed of livestock guardian dog. It was bred in the Soviet Union from about 1920 from dogs of the Caucasus Mountains and the steppe regions of Southern Russia.
Covered in coarse black hair but bare-faced, this great ape is humans' closest living relative according to fossil and DNA evidence, and lives in groups of up to 150 — which species?
Chimpanzee: Species of great ape. The chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes), also simply known as the chimp, is a medium-sized great ape species found in the forests and savannas of equatorial Africa.
Sold as Catapres and Kapvay, this drug treats high blood pressure, ADHD, and drug-withdrawal symptoms, and can be delivered via a skin patch — what is it?
Renowned for a gift of mimicry noted by Pliny the Elder and Shakespeare, this glossy black bird has a bill that turns from black in winter to yellow in summer — what species is it?
Common starling: Species of passerine birds.

This academic framework examines how systemic bias against certain ethnic groups is embedded in laws and institutions, using the concept of intersectionality to explain overlapping forms of inequality — what is it called?
Critical race theory: Conceptual framework. The word critical in the name is an academic reference to critical theory, not criticizing or blaming individuals.

Dubbed the 'father of modern experimental optics,' this Scottish inventor discovered the angle and the photoelasticity that bear on polarized light — and improved the stereoscope along the way. Who was he?
David Brewster: British astronomer and mathematician (1781–1868)
Sold as Benadryl, this first-generation H1-antihistamine is famously sedating — yet at higher doses it can paradoxically cause agitation and restlessness instead of sleep; what's the drug?
Diphenhydramine: Antihistamine medication. Diphenhydramine, sold under the brand name Benadryl among others, is an antihistamine and sedative.
Named for its 'skin wings,' this insect order sports pincer-like cerci on its abdomen and displays unusually attentive maternal care for its young — which insect?
Earwig: Order of insects. Damage to foliage, flowers, and various crops is commonly blamed on earwigs, especially the common earwig Forficula auricularia.

Distinguished by its massive head, huge size, and trademark black facial mask, this gentle British dog breed is now classed as vulnerable in its homeland, with just 104 UK births recorded in 2020 — which breed?
English Mastiff: British breed of dog. The English Mastiff, or simply the Mastiff, is a British breed of very large dog of mastiff type.
This small European finch's male sports a blue-grey cap and rust-red underparts, while both sexes flash white wing bars — what species is it?
Eurasian chaffinch: Species of bird. The Eurasian chaffinch, common chaffinch, or simply the chaffinch (Fringilla coelebs) is a common and widespread small passerine bird – in the finch family.
Native to North African deserts from Western Sahara to the Sinai, this diminutive canid uses its oversized ears to shed heat and detect prey burrowing underground — which species is it?
Fennec fox: Species of fox. The fennec fox (Vulpes zerda) is a small fox native to the deserts of North Africa, ranging from Western Sahara and Mauritania to the Sinai Peninsula.
A pungent colorless gas churned out at 26 million tons a year, it's used to make resins and, in a roughly 37% solution, to preserve tissue samples in labs — what is it?

Marked by heartburn, regurgitation, and even dental corrosion from stomach acid creeping back up the digestive tract, this chronic condition can, if untreated, lead to esophageal stricture or Barrett's esophagus — what is it?
Gastroesophageal reflux disease: Flow of stomach contents into the esophagus.
Occurring mainly in the liver, this metabolic pathway builds new glucose from non-carbohydrate sources to help prevent low blood sugar — what is it called?
This Dutch programmer created a popular programming language and held the title 'benevolent dictator for life' until stepping down in 2018. Who is he?
Guido van Rossum: Dutch programmer and creator of Python (born 1956)
Tapeworms, flukes and roundworms all fall under this broad name for any infection where parasitic worms take up residence in the body. What is the condition called?
Helminthiasis: Any macroparasitic disease caused by helminths.
Belonging to the genus Apis, this eusocial insect builds perennial nests of hexagonal wax cells and stores surplus food as a prized sweet — which creature is it?
This condition, caused by low blood potassium below 3.5 mmol/L, can bring on fatigue, leg cramps, and a dangerously slow heart rhythm — what is it?
Hypokalemia: Insufficient potassium in the blood. Normal potassium levels in humans are between 3.5 and 5.0 mmol/L (3.5 and 5.0 mEq/L) with levels below 3.5 mmol/L defined as hypokalemia.
Discovered by Bernard Courtois in 1811, this heaviest stable halogen melts to a deep violet liquid and is the heaviest essential nutrient — needed to make thyroid hormones. What element is it?
Iodine: Chemical element with atomic number 53 (I)
Enlisting disguised as a man named 'Jean' on Bougainville's expedition, this expert botanist became the first woman to circumnavigate the globe — who is she?
Jeanne Baret: French explorer, naturalist, botanist (1740–1807)

This Indian aerospace engineer led the nation's space agency as chairman and served as secretary of the Department of Space, after directing both the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre and the Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre — who is he?
These paired skin folds run from the mons pubis to the perineum and are considered the anatomical counterpart to the male scrotum — what are they called?
Labia majora: Folds of skin that contain and protect the vulva's other parts.

Elon Musk's praise for his MIT driver-attention study on Tesla's autopilot brought this computer scientist to prominence in 2019, ahead of a career hosting long-form interviews with notable figures — who is he?
Lex Fridman: American scientist and podcast host (born 1983)
Sold as Ativan, this benzodiazepine treats anxiety, insomnia, and active seizures, and is even used during surgery to interfere with memory formation — what medication is it?
Lorazepam: Benzodiazepine medication. Lorazepam, sold under the brand name Ativan among others, is a benzodiazepine medication.
This genus of some 32 to 57 deciduous tree and shrub species in the rose family includes the domesticated orchard fruit tree along with crab and wild varieties — what genus is it?
Malus: Flowering genus, rose family Rosaceae.
Originally designated the DC-9 Series 80, this five-abreast single-aisle airliner first flew in October 1979 and entered service with launch customer Swissair the following year — what jet is it?
McDonnell Douglas MD-80: Jet airliner model, series based on the DC-9.

This American climatologist pioneered techniques to pull climate signals from noisy data, building a famous reconstruction of the past thousand years' temperatures with two co-authors in 1998 — who is he?
Michael E. Mann: American physicist and climatologist. Michael Evan Mann (born 1965) is an American climatologist and geophysicist.
Discovered in 1778 by Carl Wilhelm Scheele and boasting the sixth-highest melting point of any element, this metal is mostly used in steel alloys — what is it?
Molybdenum: Chemical element with atomic number 42 (Mo)

It strikes when blood flow to the heart muscle stops, killing tissue — classically a crushing chest pain that radiates to the left arm or jaw, though women more often feel only neck pain or fatigue. What is this medical emergency?
Myocardial infarction: Interruption of cardiac blood supply.
A vitamer of vitamin B3 that the body can build from tryptophan, in large prescription doses it lowers LDL and raises "good" HDL cholesterol — what's this compound also called niacin?
Nicotinic acid: Organic compound and a form of vitamin B3.

Symbolized by the Greek letter omega, this SI unit of electrical resistance was named after a 19th-century German physicist and, since 2019, is defined as an exact value based on fundamental constants — what unit is it?
Ohm: SI derived unit of electrical resistance. The ohm (symbol: Ω, the uppercase Greek letter omega) is the unit of electrical resistance in the International System of Units (SI).
Making up most of Earth's crust, this class of chemical compound pairs oxygen with another element — the same chemistry behind the thin protective layer on aluminium foil — what is it called?
Oxide: Compounds containing an oxygen atom.
First domesticated in Neolithic China, this tree's fruit comes in a fuzzy form and a glossy-skinned twin called the nectarine — what fruit, a rose-family relative of the cherry and plum?
Peach: Type of fruit tree, or its fruit.
Sold under brand names like Sudafed PE, this nasal decongestant works as a selective alpha-1 adrenergic receptor agonist — what is the drug?
Phenylephrine: Decongestant medication. It is unclear whether its use during pregnancy and breastfeeding is safe.
First classified as its own fossil order in 1835, this group of Mesozoic marine reptiles thrived through the Jurassic before dying out at the end of the Cretaceous — what are they called?
Plesiosaur: Order of reptiles (fossil). The Plesiosauria or plesiosaurs are an order or clade of extinct Mesozoic marine reptiles, belonging to the Sauropterygia.
This New World family within the order Carnivora encompasses raccoons, ringtails, coatis, and kinkajous, most of them omnivorous — what family is it?
Procyonidae: Family of mammals. Procyonidae ( PROH-see-ON-i-dee) is a New World family of the order Carnivora.
Native to southern China, this pear tree's fruit goes by dozens of names worldwide - Asian pear, apple pear, nashi pear - but is rarely baked into pies due to its high water content - which species?
Pyrus pyrifolia: Species of pear with round crisp grainy fruit.
Rooted in Minangkabau cooking at the crossroads of the Malacca Strait, this dish slow-cooks meat in spiced coconut milk until the oil separates and it fries in its own glaze — what is it?

Nicknamed the 'dark lady of DNA,' this X-ray crystallographer's crucial contributions to the discovery of DNA's structure went largely unrecognized in her lifetime — James Watson believed she'd have won a Nobel Prize had she lived. Who was she?
Also called Besnier–Boeck–Schaumann disease, this non-infectious condition forms clusters of inflammatory cells called granulomata, often starting in the lungs, skin, or lymph nodes — what is it?
Sarcoidosis: Abnormal formation of clumps of inflammatory cells (granulomata)
About 90% of this mood-regulating neurotransmitter is actually made in your gut, where it controls intestinal movement, rather than the brain — also known as 5-HT, what is it?
Serotonin: Monoamine neurotransmitter. It is involved in mood, cognition, reward, learning, memory, and physiological processes such as vomiting and vasoconstriction.
Coined in the late 18th century, this social science studies human society — from one-on-one interactions to sweeping social structures and everyday culture. What is it?
Sociology: Scientific study of human society and relationships.
